06/ 16.01.2024 Heard learned senior counsel for the appellant and the learned cou for the State on the prayer for suspension of sentence made on behalf of the appellant through I.A.
No. 809 of 2023.
2.

Learned senior counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant has been convicted for the offence under section 376(DA) of the Indian Penal Code and section 6 of POCSO Act on the allegation of committing rape of a minor girl aged 15 years.
Learned counsel has further stated that the victim has been examined as P.W-1.
She has not stated anything about commission of rape by this appellant in the FIR.
Even in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr. P.C, she has not stated that the appellant has committed rape upon her.
It has been further submitted that even in her deposition, she has stated that the appellant had caught hold of her while she was subjected to rape by the co- accused.
However, there is no such statement made in the FIR or under section 164 Cr. P.C, which raises doubt on the prosecution case.

While referring to the statement made in para-28 and 30 of her cross-examination, learned counsel submitted that there is complete denial by the victim that this appellant and co- accused had committed rape upon her.
Learned counsel has referred to the deposition of the I.O which suggest that there is no evidence that this appellant had gone to the house of the victim.
Learned counsel has further submitted that the appellant is in custody since 01.06.2019.
Therefore, considering the period of custody, appellant may be allowed the privilege of suspension of sentence.
3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail and submits that the victim is a minor girl of 15 years of age.

She has clearly stated in the FIR as well as in her statement recorded under section 164 of the Cr. P.C. about the presence of this appellant at the time and place of occurrence and facilitated the co-accused in commission of rape upon her.

The doctor in his medical Sanjay Mahli vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53678928/
1 report has clearly opined that there was abrasion and bleeding on the person of the victim which could suggest that force was used against the victim.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per section 376(DA) of the Indian Penal Code, if a person is present and facilitate others in commission of the crime, he cannot be allowed to go Scott free.
Based on these submissions, learned counsel for the State prays that appellant should not be allowed the privilege of suspension of sentence.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the lower court records, we are not inclined to enlarge the appellant on bail.
Accordingly, his prayer for bail stands rejected.

5. I.A. No. 809 of 2023 stands rejected (Ratnaker Bhengra, J) (Ambuj Nath, J) Ranjeet/ Uploaded Sanjay Mahli vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53678928/
